what: bass-digital rendered through the real AudioWorklet in Chrome (OfflineAudioContext, 48 kHz, 51,200 frames, note 60 @ velocity 0.9, noteOff at frame 12,000) — the same signal the Node harness in fmProcessor.test.ts renders, so the two can be compared sample-peak to sample-peak.
how: chrome-devtools MCP evaluate_script on the ?debug=1 page: import('/src/audio/presets.ts'), OfflineAudioContext.audioWorklet.addModule('/src/audio/worklet/fm-processor.js'), new AudioWorkletNode(ctx, 'fm-part', { processorOptions: { maxVoices: 16, patch, events, seed? } }).
reads: seed7_a === seed7_b on both pages: the same seed is the same audio in a real AudioWorklet, not only under the Node shim.
seed8 differs from seed7: the seed is actually driving the draws.
unseeded_a !== unseeded_b on both pages: with no seed the processor still free-runs from Math.random, which is the game path and is unchanged.
defaultSeed_0xa204 and worstPhases match the Node harness to 4 decimals, so the harness's numbers are the browser's numbers and the 6.1% headroom is not an artefact of the shim.
The render is audio-only and identical across the two rendering backends, as expected: the AudioWorklet does not touch the GPU.
